plan.contextChunk: This figure graphs a single upward-opening parabola on a coordinate plane and annotates its main features with labeled arrows. Both axes are numbered from -6 to 6 over a dotted gray grid, with x labeled at the right end of the horizontal axis and y at the top of the vertical one. The curve is a heavy teal U with arrowheads on both rising branches; its lowest point sits at x equal to 1, y equal to -4, and the branches climb to about y equal to 5 near x equal to -2 on the left and x equal to 4 on the right. Small filled dots mark the two crossings of the x-axis at x equal to -1 and x equal to 3, the crossing of the y-axis at y equal to -3, the turning point, and the mirror partner of the y-intercept at x equal to 2. A red dashed vertical line runs through x equal to 1, reached by an arrow from the label Axis of symmetry above. Three further labels point to the graph and read x-intercepts, y-intercept, and Vertex. Drawing the dashed line through the turning point lets the reader check that the marked dots sit at equal heights on either side. The graph fixes the vocabulary for reading a quadratic.

interactionPlan.concept: Every feature of a parabola — vertex, axis of symmetry, intercepts — is determined by its equation, so moving the vertex moves the symmetry line and changing the vertical stretch respaces the intercepts.

axis labels 'x' at right end of horizontal axis and 'y' at top of vertical axis
teal upward-opening parabola y = (x - 1)^2 - 4 with arrowheads on both rising branches
red dashed vertical axis of symmetry at x = 1, with label 'Axis of symmetry' and pointer arrow
black dot at the vertex (1, -4), with label 'Vertex' and pointer arrow
black dots at the x-intercepts (-1, 0) and (3, 0), with label 'x-intercepts' and pointer arrows
black dot at the y-intercept (0, -3), with label 'y-intercept' and pointer arrow
black dot at the mirror partner of the y-intercept (2, -3)

interactions.teaches: The vertex is the anchor of the parabola: dragging it moves the axis of symmetry, the intercepts, and every paired point together, showing the vertex fixes both the turning point and the symmetry line

interactions.label: Vertical stretch a
interactions.teaches: The leading coefficient controls how fast the branches rise: larger a pulls the x-intercepts closer together, smaller a spreads them apart, while the axis of symmetry and vertex stay fixed

interactions.label: Highlight features
interactions.teaches: Switching emphasis ties each vocabulary term to its visible feature: intercepts are axis crossings, and the vertex, axis line, y-intercept, and its mirror point are all reflections about the symmetry line

demo_steps.title: Read the features
demo_steps.narration: The parabola y = (x − 1)² − 4 shows all key features at once: vertex at (1, −4), axis of symmetry x = 1, x-intercepts at −1 and 3, y-intercept at −3 and its mirror point at (2, −3).

demo_steps.title: Check the symmetry
demo_steps.narration: Highlighting the symmetry markers shows the y-intercept and its mirror point sit at equal heights on opposite sides of the dashed line, equally far from x = 1 — the defining test of the axis of symmetry.

demo_steps.title: Drag the vertex
demo_steps.narration: Drag the vertex to a new location: the dashed axis of symmetry, both intercepts, and the mirror pair all travel with it — the vertex alone determines where the symmetry line lies.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the parabola
demo_steps.narration: Increase a and the branches steepen, pulling the x-intercepts inward toward the axis; decrease a and they spread outward. The vertex and axis of symmetry never move.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The vertex determines the axis of symmetry, and the vertical stretch determines how far the x-intercepts sit from that axis — two parameters completely fix the parabola's geometry.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Coordinate plane spanning -6 to 6 on both axes with light dotted gray gridlines at integers; axes drawn as solid black lines with arrowheads. Parabola is a heavy teal curve opening upward with arrowheads at the tops of both branches, defaulting to y = (x−1)² − 4 (vertex (1,−4), x-intercepts −1 and 3, y-intercept −3, branch tops near y = 5 at x = −2 and x = 4). Red dashed vertical line through the vertex, full height of the plot. Filled black dots at vertex, both x-intercepts, y-intercept, and mirror point. Labels 'Axis of symmetry', 'x-intercepts', 'y-intercept', 'Vertex' with thin leader arrows, positioned as in the original (axis label upper right, x-intercepts label right, y-intercept and Vertex labels lower area). Dragging the vertex re-forms the curve as y = a(x−h)² + k in real time; the stretch slider changes a only. In highlight modes, non-emphasized labels and dots fade to gray while emphasized ones stay full black/red.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Drag for moving the vertex; the learner drags the parabola's lowest point, the dashed axis of symmetry and paired points move with it, and it becomes clear that the vertex fixes both the turning point and the symmetry line.
- Slider for vertical stretch; the learner changes the parabola's opening width, the x-intercepts move closer together or farther apart while the axis stays fixed, and the relationship between the quadratic coefficient and intercept spacing becomes clear.

authoredContext:
The graph of a quadratic function is a U-shaped curve called a parabola. One important feature of the graph is that it has an extreme point, called the vertex. If the parabola opens up, the vertex represents the lowest point on the graph, or the minimum value of the quadratic function. If the parabola opens down, the vertex represents the highest point on the graph, or the maximum value. In either case, the vertex is a turning point on the graph. The graph is also symmetric with a vertical line drawn through the vertex, called the axis of symmetry. These features are illustrated in the figure.

Graph of a parabola showing where the x and y intercepts, vertex, and axis of symmetry are.

The y-intercept is the point at which the parabola crosses the y-axis. The x-intercepts are the points at which the parabola crosses the x-axis. If they exist, the x-intercepts represent the zeros, or roots, of the quadratic function, the values of x at which y=0.

discrepancies: The generated figure crashes on load: the screenshot shows only an 'Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'data')' error overlay and no chart at all, so none of the source content (parabola, vertex, intercepts, axis of symmetry) is visible

Root cause in code: the custom 'annotate' plugin's afterDraw fires during the initial render inside the `new Chart(...)` constructor, before the `chart` variable is assigned, so getDs('curve') reads chart.data on an undefined reference and the whole render throws
evaluation.notes: The design (vertex-form parabola with labeled vertex, intercepts, dashed axis of symmetry, drag/slider/demo-step interactions) is faithful in intent, but a plugin-afterDraw-vs-constructor timing bug crashes the figure on load, leaving only an error overlay instead of the source graph.
action_items: Guard the annotate plugin against the constructor-time call: either skip drawing until `chart` is assigned (e.g. `if (!chart || !chart.scales || !chart.scales.x) return;` inside drawAnnotations/getDs) or reference the plugin's own chart argument `c` (c.data, c.scales) instead of the outer `chart` variable.

After the fix, verify the default step-0 state actually draws the parabola y = (x − 1)² − 4 with vertex dot, both x-intercept dots, y-intercept dot, red dashed axis of symmetry, and all four source labels.
Confirm the vertex-drag, vertical-stretch slider, and highlight dropdown redraw after the crash fix, since none of them could execute while the initial render threw.

discrepancies: The source uses free-floating x and y axes with bold arrowheads crossing at the origin, while the generated figure draws a boxed Chart.js plot frame with the axes only as frame borders — the x-axis no longer runs through y = 0 as in the source

The source's 'Axis of symmetry' annotation sits at the top with a diagonal leader pointing to the dashed line; the generated leader points down to about y = 2, which is acceptable, but the label is cramped against the top edge of the plot
The source shows coarse gridlines at every integer with labeled ticks every 2 units; the generated grid matches the tick step (2), slightly coarsening the graph-paper feel
The equation readout 'y = 1(x − 1)² − 4' is an added annotation not present in the source and shows a redundant leading '1'
evaluation.notes: All five features (vertex, axis of symmetry, both x-intercepts, y-intercept and its mirror point) are correctly placed at (1,−4), x = 1, −1/3, −3/(2,−3) with the teal curve and red dashed axis closely matching the source; the main visual departure is the boxed Chart.js frame replacing the open arrow-tipped axes, and interactions (drag-vertex, stretch slider, highlight toggle, 4-step demo) are rich and functional.
action_items: Suppress the '1' in the equation readout when a = 1 so it renders 'y = (x − 1)² − 4' instead of 'y = 1(x − 1)² − 4'
Approximate the source's open axes: hide the boxed frame and draw the x-axis through y = 0 and y-axis through x = 0 with arrowheads instead of relying on Chart.js scale borders
Increase grid density to every 1 unit (minor gridlines) to match the source's graph-paper look
Move the 'Axis of symmetry' label slightly lower/right so it does not sit flush against the top plot edge

feedback.rationale: No failure modes, all scores 4–5 with concept and interactivity at 5; the remaining discrepancies (boxed frame, grid density, equation formatting) are minor cosmetic deviations that do not impede understanding, so the figure is good enough to stop.
